title: [Bug] First message to picortex bot on a brand-new DM gets no reply (discovery race)
description:
Symptom (Jacob, 2026-04-23): DMing picortex@bot.globalbr.ai on chat.globalbr.ai for the first time, the bot does NOT reply. The SECOND message reliably gets a reply. Jacob suspected a timing issue.

Root cause: CONFIRMED — conversation-discovery race.

Evidence (replicated 2026-04-24 03:37-03:38 UTC):
- Fresh test user e2e_fresh_1777001825 creates NEW DM with bot via POST /api/chat/conversations (participantIds=['picortex_bot_...'], type='direct'). Convo id: bFh8_dWEIXwNvNEH3hwJF.
- Tester immediately sends 'FIRST msg' (message id qXVCMaK2THy3zKYZMPtUT). Broadcast via io.to('conversation:bFh8...').emit('message:new', ...). Bot is NOT in that room yet → not delivered.
- ~2s later picortex's 30s poll fires (03:37:47), sees the new convo (total 3→4), emits conversation:join, enters the room.
- Tester sends 'SECOND msg' at 03:38:00 (id 3uUODTcqrOLrrFa3cpdUb). Bot receives it and replies 2s later with 'Hey! Got your message. What can I help you with?'.
- picortex journalctl confirms: the first message id NEVER appears in logs; the second message id does. Bot-side socket only received the convo it just joined.

Root cause in code
- server/src/websocket/chatHandler.ts message:send handler (line 148): io.to('conversation:' + conversationId).emit('message:new', message). Only sockets that have previously called conversation:join are in the room.
- server/src/routes/chat.ts POST /conversations (lines 66-138): creates Conversation + PARTICIPATES_IN edges, returns 201. NO socket emit to notify the other participants that they are now in a new conversation.
- No conversation:created, conversation:new, or participant:added event exists on the socket server.
- Bot-side mitigation is a 30s poll (OpenChat-3ld: 'Periodic re-poll every 30s for newly-added conversations'), which creates a 0-30s window where the first message is silently dropped.

Proposed fix (server side — this ticket)
- In chat.ts POST /conversations: after CREATE, for each participant, io.to(<their user room / sockets>).emit('conversation:created', conversation) — or emit 'participant:added' to each participant.
- Options for addressing sockets per user: (a) have every socket join a 'user:${userId}' room on connect in chatHandler.ts, then emit io.to('user:' + participantId); (b) iterate userSockets map.
- Consider same event for 'add participant to existing conversation' flow (groups) once that UI ships — solves the same race for groups.
- Optionally: also buffer/retry the initial message:send if it finds zero room members who are actual participants — but the proper fix is the event.

Proposed fix (bot side — track via OpenChat-3ld)
- picortex listens for conversation:created / participant:added; on receipt, immediately GET conversation and emit conversation:join before any message arrives.
- Keep the 30s poll as a fallback.

Repro script
- /Users/Jacob/code/picortex/.claude/worktrees/agent-a8b9f846/scripts/e2e-openchat-new-convo.mjs
- Env: OPENCHAT_JWT_SECRET, TESTER_USER_ID, TESTER_EMAIL, BOT_USER_ID (default picortex_bot_7ecd2883dbd5ceef). Use a FRESH tester user that has no prior conversation with the bot (create in Neo4j first).
- Verdict field 'hypothesis_confirmed' prints true when first msg gets no reply and second msg does.

Related tickets
- OpenChat-3ld (picortex OpenChatChannel impl; v0.2 bullet listens for conversation:added — this is that event, needs server side)
- OpenChat-aoy (Group chats validation — same race affects adding bot to existing group)
- OpenChat-8bk (picortex bot user flow)
- OpenChat-qz0 (Add connection recovery for missed messages — related but not the same issue)

root_cause_confirmed: yes

title: Alice (web client) stuck in 'Reconnecting...' loop; bot doesn't reply in affected sessions
description:
Repro: Jacob signs in as Alice on chat.globalbr.ai; UI shows 'Reconnecting...' badge continuously; bot ('picortex@bot.globalbr.ai') doesn't reply in DMs even though human↔human chat appears to work.

Server logs (sudo docker logs openchat_app) show rapid connect/disconnect pairs for the same userId with different socket IDs — pattern: User connected → User disconnected within sub-second gaps. This repeats indefinitely. Not caused by the OpenChat-09h deploy — pre-existing (logs show this pattern among MULTIPLE users not just Alice).

Likely root cause: client uses transports: ['websocket', 'polling'] (see client/src/hooks/useChatSocket.ts:31). Cloudflare's proxy breaks socket.io polling fallback — the polling cycle of 'connect, XHR, close, new connect' is probably looking like real disconnects on server side. picortex bot hit the same bug and switched to transports: ['websocket']-only on 2026-04-23; fix verified empirically.

Fix to try first:
1. client/src/hooks/useChatSocket.ts: change transports to ['websocket'] only (same as picortex OpenChatChannel). If WS fails, error visibly rather than silently degrading to polling.
2. Ensure Cloudflare WebSocket upgrade is enabled for chat.globalbr.ai (should be — Noos works fine)
3. If still reconnecting: add socket.io debug logging + inspect the disconnect reason ('transport close', 'ping timeout', etc.)

Bot-not-replying angle: if user is in a DM with picortex@bot that was created BEFORE picortex-6bw / OpenChat-09h deploy, the bot should still be joined to it from picortex's 30s poll — but if the openchat socket is unstable as above, message:new broadcasts may not reach the bot either. This ticket is likely the root cause of multiple bot-not-replying reports.
close_reason: Shipped ws-only transport fix (6f229af). Verified: 0 disconnect events for picortex_bot in 2-minute post-deploy log window; pre-fix logs showed continuous sub-second connect/disconnect churn. Also added connect_error + disconnect-reason console logging for future visibility.

title: publish-to-testers.py: builds get dropped from beta review queue (timeout-poll regression)
description:
## Symptom

Build 64 (v0.1.12, uploaded 2026-06-03 14:54 UTC via the new SSH-only local-build pipeline) was assigned to Friends & Family group but NEVER submitted for Apple Beta App Review. As a result it's invisible to external testers — they're stuck on the previous approved build.

In the terminal session where this happened, publish-to-testers.py printed:
```
publish-to-testers: v0.1.12 (newest existing build: 48 uploaded 2026-06-03T11:15:16)
  no newer VALID build yet; sleeping...
  [repeat 50x]
ERROR: no newer VALID build appeared after 600s — skipping
```

It timed out waiting for a newer-than-build-48 build to appear, then exited without submitting anything. By the time build 64 hit VALID in ASC, the script had already given up.

## Root cause hypothesis

The script's poll-for-new-build logic is fragile:
1. It records 'newest existing VALID build at script start' (build 48 in this case)
2. Polls every 12s for up to 600s waiting for a build whose uploadedDate > that floor to reach VALID
3. If the freshly-uploaded build is still processing at the end of the window, the script gives up — and there's no retry / catch-up

This happens when:
- Apple's ASC build processing is slow (sometimes >10 min for fresh uploads)
- The script was invoked before the upload had fully landed (race)
- The build script in the wrapper invoked publish-to-testers.py too early

## Fix

Several options:
1. Extend POLL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS from 600 to e.g. 1800 (more lenient)
2. Pass the target build number to publish-to-testers.py explicitly when invoking from local-build.sh (we know what number we just submitted)
3. Make publish-to-testers.py idempotent and re-run-able — if a build that's still missing from F&F + beta review when invoked, do the work; otherwise no-op. Then schedule it to run periodically (cron or post-poll loop) for the most recent N unprocessed builds.
4. Add a catch-up step: when build N+1 is uploaded, also check build N still exists in the queue; if not, retroactively submit it.

Recommend (2) + (3): explicit-build-number arg + idempotent.

## Acceptance

- [ ] publish-to-testers.py accepts an optional --build-number arg; when present, skips the poll and operates on that build directly
- [ ] local-build.sh extracts the build number from the EAS build output and passes it to publish-to-testers.py
- [ ] publish-to-testers.py is idempotent — re-running on an already-assigned + already-submitted build is a clean no-op (already partially true; verify)
- [ ] Add a 'catch-up' command: scripts/publish-to-testers.py --catch-up — finds any VALID builds in ASC from the last 7 days that aren't in F&F + don't have a beta review submission, and submits them

## Impact

This blocks every local build from reaching external testers if Apple's processing is slow. Hit once today (build 64) and visible in the audit. Almost certainly hit other times we didn't notice.

## Related

- Closed bug OpenChat-ert (Albert SIWA — actually was build-30-related, not a SIWA config bug, partially because of this issue)
- bd memory proactive-error-monitoring-after-deploy
- scripts/local-build.sh — calling code

title: In-app Feedback channel — built-in DM-able support thread
description:
## What

Every OpenChat user gets a pre-populated 'Feedback' conversation pinned at the top of their conversation list. They can send messages, screenshots, voice notes, etc. directly to it. Jacob (or a small team) receives those messages and can respond. Acts as both bug reporter, feature requester, and warm-touch support channel.

## Why

- Lowers friction to reporting bugs vs 'go to a webpage and fill a form'
- Captures attachments/voice naturally (the app already supports them)
- Builds product intuition by seeing real-user complaints in the same UX they use
- For a small early-stage app this is much higher value than a generic /feedback URL

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On new account create, auto-create a 'Feedback' conversation between the user and a designated Feedback bot/admin user (Jacob's account, or a dedicated 'feedback@openchat' user)
- [ ] Conversation pinned to top of conversation list (or shown in a special slot)
- [ ] Conversation marked with a distinct UI affordance ('💬 Feedback' icon + label)
- [ ] First message is a templated welcome from the bot ('Hi — what's working, what's broken, what do you wish OpenChat did?')
- [ ] Sender (Jacob) can reply, attaching screenshots/voice
- [ ] Admin view shows aggregate feedback across users (a feed of all Feedback threads sorted by recency)

## Design decisions

- Is it 1-on-1 (user ↔ Jacob) or a group chat with multiple supporters? → 1-on-1 with Jacob's account for v1
- Existing users (pre-launch): batch-create Feedback threads for everyone who already has an account
- Should the bot send periodic check-ins (e.g. 'how's it going?' after 7 days)? Defer to v2
- Should there be an opt-out? No (it's just a chat; user can mute or delete it)

## Open

- Does Jacob want his real account to receive these, or a dedicated 'feedback' user with shared inbox?
- Is there a 'set message read' or autoresponder pattern to prevent users feeling ignored?
notes:
## DESIGN LOCKED 2026-06-03

Jacob: 'I want a dedicated feedback user.'

Implementation: server creates a special User node (id: 'feedback', or similar reserved id; email like 'feedback@openchat' or no email; display name 'OpenChat Feedback' with a distinct avatar). Every new account gets an auto-created conversation between them and this user.

A small support team (Jacob + future help) can have admin access to read all conversations involving the feedback user — a 'shared inbox' view. That admin UI is out of scope for v1 — for v1 Jacob can just sign in AS the feedback user via a server-side magic link to triage manually. Build the proper shared-inbox UX once the volume justifies it.

Schema sketch:
- User node with id='feedback' (reserved), flag isSystemUser=true
- On signup hook: auto-create a 1:1 conversation between new user and feedback user
- Pin the conversation in the conversation list (server-side flag + client respects it)
- First message from feedback user templated: 'Hi — what's working, what's broken, what do you wish OpenChat did?'
- Admin access: Jacob's account has a flag isAdmin=true that grants read access to all conversations involving the feedback user (cypher query: MATCH (admin:User {isAdmin:true})-[:HAS_VIEW_ACCESS]->(c:Conversation) ... or similar)

Open: how does Jacob authenticate AS the feedback user to reply? Options:
- Magic JWT swap from admin account (one-click 'reply as feedback user')
- A second auth method bound to the feedback user (linked to Jacob's email)
- A simple admin UI that posts to the conversation as the feedback user

For v1: magic JWT swap is fastest.

title: Identity & discovery — multi-auth login, phone/email identifiers, contact-based finding
description:
## What

Make OpenChat aware of phone-number identity so friends can find each other automatically and so users have an alternative signup to Apple/Google/email. Three layered sub-features that build on each other:

### Sub-feature 1 — Phone number as profile field
Foundation. Let users add a phone number to their profile (E.164, server-validated). No verification required at this layer. Just a string field on the User node. Enables sub-features 2 + 3 to function.

### Sub-feature 2 — Contacts permission → hashed friend-discovery
Request iOS Contacts permission (with clear copy). On grant, hash phone numbers + emails client-side (SHA-256 of E.164-normalized number + lowercased email). Send batches of hashes to server. Server returns matches of users already on OpenChat. Show 'people you may know' list with start-chat affordance.

Privacy choices:
- Hashed lookup (never send raw contacts) — recommended
- Optional 'reveal me to people who have my number' toggle (opt-in to BE discovered)
- Never persist contact hashes server-side beyond the lookup request

### Sub-feature 3 — Phone-number signup
Alternative to Apple/Google. Twilio (or MessageBird / Vonage) SMS OTP flow. New screens: PhoneEntryScreen → OTPEntryScreen → ProfileSetupScreen. Server endpoints: POST /api/auth/phone/send-otp, POST /api/auth/phone/verify. Stores hashed-and-salted phone, links to User.

## Sequencing

1 → 2 → 3. Sub 1 is cheap and unblocks the rest. Sub 2 has high user value once 1 ships. Sub 3 is biggest scope (SMS provider account, OTP storage, anti-abuse).

## Open design questions

- Phone field visibility: public profile? friends only? hidden by default?
- SMS provider: Twilio is default; cost considerations for scaling
- OTP delivery: SMS only, or also WhatsApp / push to existing OpenChat install?
- International support from day 1 or US-only MVP?
- Anti-abuse: per-IP / per-number rate limits, CAPTCHA gate, max sends per day
- Privacy posture: opt-in discoverability vs default discoverable

## Related

- OpenChat-d8w (App Privacy nutrition labels) — will need updates when each sub ships
- The existing 4-permission PermissionsScreen will gain a Contacts row
notes:
## DESIGN REFINEMENT 2026-06-03 (Jacob)

Original epic was scoped to 'contacts + phone'. After review, the scope broadens to the full identity layer:

1. **Phone is ENCOURAGED, not required at signup.** New users get a UI nudge to add a phone, but can skip. (Adjusts 3ag.3 framing.)

2. **Multi-auth: many login methods per account, all linkable.** A user's account isn't tied to ONE auth provider — they can have Apple + Google + phone + email all bound to the same account, and use any to sign in. Add provider-linking as a first-class concept. (New: 3ag.4.)

3. **Manual identifier addition.** Users should be able to attach an email (or other identifier) to their account AFTER signup — not just at signup — so others can find them by it. e.g. signed up with phone, later add 'jacob@idea.io' for email-based discovery. (New: 3ag.5.)

4. **Per-identifier searchability, default ON.** For each identifier (phone, email, future others) a user has, there's an independent 'others can find me by this' toggle. Default ON for new identifiers — users can flip individual ones off without disabling all discovery. (New: 3ag.6.)

5. **Passkey login as future work.** Plan for WebAuthn/passkey as a future auth method that fits the multi-auth model — no MVP commitment, but architect 3ag.4 to accommodate it. (New: 3ag.7, deferred.)

## Updated sequencing

3ag.1 (phone field as part of a generalized 'identifiers' concept) →
3ag.4 (multi-auth + linking framework) →
3ag.5 (post-signup manual identifier addition) →
3ag.6 (per-identifier searchability) →
3ag.2 (contacts-based friend discovery, USING the identifiers from above) →
3ag.3 (phone-based signup, with 'encouraged but skippable' framing) →
3ag.7 (passkey, future-deferred)

3ag.4 becomes the cornerstone: once multi-auth + linking works, everything else slots in.

title: Phone number as user profile field (foundation for contacts+phone epic)
description:
## What

Add an optional phone number to the User profile. E.164 format (+15551234567). Server-side validation (regex + libphonenumber-style normalization). UI to set/clear from ProfileEditScreen.

This is the foundation that unlocks both Contacts-based friend discovery (sub 2) and phone-based signup (sub 3) — both need users to have a phone number associated with their account to function.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] User node has optional `phone` field (E.164 string)
- [ ] Server normalizes + validates phone on set (rejects non-E.164)
- [ ] ProfileEditScreen has 'Phone' row with country code picker
- [ ] Empty value allowed — phone is optional, not required
- [ ] Phone shown on own profile (always visible to self)
- [ ] Phone visibility on others' profiles: default HIDDEN (revealed later in sub 2)
- [ ] Server endpoint: PATCH /api/users/me with phone field
- [ ] Validation error returned cleanly (400 with reason)

## Open

- Server: should phone be hashed at rest, or stored plaintext? Plaintext makes the matching easier but more sensitive. Decision: store plaintext, restrict access strictly (only self + matched contacts can read).
notes:
## Visibility decision 2026-06-03 (Jacob)

**Default phone visibility on others' profiles: HIDDEN.**

Phone is used for discovery (the contacts-hashing match in 3ag.2) but is NOT shown on other users' profile views. WhatsApp-style: invisible to randos, discoverable by people who already have the number.

Phone visible only to:
- Self (always, on own profile)
- Admin tooling (server-side)

Future consideration: friends-only visibility option — filed as separate ticket. Not in scope for v1.

title: Username/handle as user-visible identifier — expose, allow edit, search-by-handle, @-mention
description:
## Why

Jacob 2026-06-03: 'I want a username ultimately, as long as it doesn't get annoying. You shouldn't need to remember to sign in or something.'

Username already exists on the User node (column 'username') and is auto-populated from email local-part at signup (e.g. tmad4000@gmail.com → username 'tmad4000'). Dedup is done by appending a numeric suffix when there's a collision (e.g. 'test', 'test1'). But the username is invisible everywhere user-facing — not on profiles, not in @-mention, not in search.

This ticket makes username a real first-class identity element WITHOUT making it a sign-in credential. Users sign in via email/Apple/Google/phone as today; username is a friendly handle that other users see and address them by.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Username shown on user profile (mine + others')
- [ ] Username settable by user via Profile → Edit (one-time per N days, or always, TBD)
- [ ] Username uniqueness enforced server-side at set time (reserved against collision)
- [ ] @-mention picker filters by username (in addition to display name)
- [ ] Search by @username in the existing search surface returns the matching user
- [ ] Username supports the same per-identifier searchability toggle (OpenChat-3ag.6) — users can opt out of being findable by their handle
- [ ] Reserved usernames (admin, system, openchat, feedback, support, etc.) cannot be claimed
- [ ] Username format: alphanumeric + underscore + hyphen, 3-30 chars, case-insensitive uniqueness (display preserves case)

## NOT in scope

- Username as a sign-in credential (sign-in stays via email/Apple/Google/phone per OpenChat-3ag.4 multi-auth)
- Username trading / marketplace
- Vanity URL / public handle pages (could be a future ticket)
- Auto-suggesting usernames during signup (defer; auto-populate from email is fine for v1)

## Open

- Migration: existing users have auto-generated usernames. Do we let them rename for free once, or grandfather them as-is and only allow new users to choose?
- Edit cadence: can change once a year? once a month? unlimited? Discord allows unlimited but with cooldown
- Collision on rename: if Jacob renames his username to one Alice already had (and Alice later deleted), is that a conflict?

## Related

- OpenChat-3ag.1 (identifier model) — username is another kind of identifier
- OpenChat-3ag.4 (multi-auth) — username is NOT an auth method
- OpenChat-3ag.6 (searchability toggles) — username gets its own toggle

title: Contacts permission + hashed friend-discovery (find people you may know)
description:
## What

Request iOS Contacts permission. Hash every contact's phone/email client-side. Send batches of hashes to server. Server returns matches of OpenChat users whose phone (from sub 1) or email matches. Show a 'People you may know' list with a tap-to-chat affordance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New PermissionsScreen row: 'Contacts' with clear copy ('to find friends already on OpenChat')
- [ ] On grant, fetch contacts via expo-contacts
- [ ] Hash each phone (after E.164 normalization) + email (lowercased) with SHA-256
- [ ] Batch hashes (e.g. 500 at a time) to POST /api/discovery/match
- [ ] Server: lookup User nodes by hashed-phone-or-email, return matching User IDs (never reveal hashes)
- [ ] Server: NEVER persist incoming hashes — match-and-discard per request
- [ ] Client: PeopleYouMayKnowScreen showing matches with avatar + name + 'Start chat' button
- [ ] Settings toggle: 'Let others find me by my phone number' (default on; disabling removes you from matches)
- [ ] Re-sync on demand from Settings (no auto re-poll; user-initiated)

## Privacy guarantees

- Raw contacts never leave the device
- Hashes are not stored server-side beyond the request lifetime
- Users can opt out of being discovered via the Settings toggle
- App Privacy nutrition labels updated when this ships (OpenChat-d8w)

## Depends on

OpenChat-3ag.1 (phone field — without it the phone-match half doesn't work; email match works on day 1)

## Open

- Default state of 'Let others find me' toggle: on (more useful) vs off (more private)
- Hash format: include a fixed salt to make rainbow-table attacks costlier? (recommend yes)
- Re-sync cadence: manual only, or daily background?
notes:
## Hash salt decision 2026-06-03 (Jacob)

**v1: fixed salt (option A).** A constant baked into both client and server (e.g., 'openchat-discovery-v1'). Simpler protocol, no extra round-trips, fine for the threat model at current scale.

Trade-off accepted: an attacker with enough compute could build a rainbow table to reverse common phone numbers from intercepted hashes. At OpenChat's current/near-term scale this is theoretical; revisit if (a) the user base grows substantially, (b) we ship a public-facing discovery API, or (c) someone publishes an attack on the fixed-salt approach.

Future consideration: per-session server-issued salt — filed as separate ticket. Not in scope for v1.

title: Phone-number signup (SMS OTP) as alternative to Apple/Google
description:
## What

Add phone-number signup/signin as a 4th option alongside Apple, Google, email. SMS-based OTP flow via Twilio (or MessageBird / Vonage). New screens: PhoneEntryScreen → OTPEntryScreen → (if new user) ProfileSetupScreen.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] PhoneEntryScreen on LoginScreen with country code picker
- [ ] POST /api/auth/phone/send-otp { phone } → sends SMS, returns request ID
- [ ] OTPEntryScreen with 6-digit code input + 'resend' affordance + countdown
- [ ] POST /api/auth/phone/verify { requestId, code } → returns OpenChat JWT + user (creates user if new)
- [ ] If new user → route to ProfileSetupScreen (name, avatar) before HomeScreen
- [ ] If existing user → straight to HomeScreen
- [ ] Anti-abuse: per-phone rate limit (3/hour), per-IP rate limit, CAPTCHA gate for high-volume IPs
- [ ] Error UX: invalid number, expired code, too many attempts
- [ ] Server: store hashed+salted OTP with TTL (10 min); never store plaintext
- [ ] Server: rotate OTP secret separately from JWT secret

## Out of scope (defer to follow-ups)

- WhatsApp delivery (use SMS only for v1)
- Voice fallback for SMS (use SMS only)
- Phone change after signup (separate flow)

## Provider choice

Twilio is the default — most mature, decent international coverage, ~$0.0075/SMS US. Alternatives: MessageBird (cheaper international, less mature), Vonage (similar to Twilio).

## Depends on

OpenChat-3ag.1 (phone field on User)
notes:
## Refinement 2026-06-03

Phone signup is ONE of many auth methods, not THE method. New framing:

- At signup the user is presented with all auth options (Apple, Google, email, phone). Phone is **encouraged** with a soft nudge ('helps friends find you') but the user can pick any method.
- After signup, additional methods can be linked via 3ag.4.
- The 'phone-required at signup' design is explicitly REJECTED. New users can complete signup via Apple-only and add a phone later if they want.

title: Multi-auth: link many login methods to one account (Apple + Google + phone + email)
description:
## What

Refactor authentication so a User can have MULTIPLE bound auth methods, not exactly one. Sign in via Apple OR Google OR phone OR email-password OR (future) passkey — all routing to the same account. From Settings, see all bound methods and link/unlink additional ones.

Today: signing in with Apple creates User A; signing in with Google creates User B; same human ends up with two separate OpenChat accounts. After this lands: same human links Apple + Google to one account, picks either to sign in.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] User node has a relationship to multiple AuthMethod nodes: (User)-[:HAS_AUTH_METHOD]->(AuthMethod {provider, providerSubject, addedAt})
- [ ] Provider types: apple, google, email, phone (more later: passkey)
- [ ] Sign-in flow lookup: 'find AuthMethod by (provider, providerSubject) → return its User'
- [ ] Account merge prevention: signing in with a new provider on an existing account adds an AuthMethod; signing in with a provider whose providerSubject is already bound to a DIFFERENT account triggers a 'merge accounts?' UX (NOT auto-merge — needs explicit user consent due to data conflicts)
- [ ] Settings → Account → 'Sign-in methods': list current + 'Add a sign-in method' button
- [ ] Add flow: user proves they own the new provider (Apple/Google/phone OTP), server attaches AuthMethod to current user
- [ ] Remove flow: cannot remove your LAST sign-in method (would lock you out); UI disables that action with explanation
- [ ] Server endpoints: GET /api/auth/methods, POST /api/auth/methods/link, DELETE /api/auth/methods/:id

## Architecture decisions

- AuthMethod is separate from Identifier (3ag.1). An AuthMethod is HOW you sign in. An Identifier is HOW others find you. Email might be both. Phone might be both. Apple subject is auth-only (not a discoverability identifier). Keep the two concepts separate but linked where appropriate.
- Migration: existing single-auth users get an AuthMethod row backfilled from their current login provider; behavior unchanged for them until they explicitly link a second method.

## Depends on

OpenChat-3ag.1 (identifiers concept — informs the schema separation)

## Out of scope (separate)

- Cross-account merge UX (the 'merge two accounts that turned out to be the same person?' flow — design deferred)
- SAML / enterprise SSO bindings — way later
notes:
## Account merge UX decision 2026-06-03 (Jacob)

**Prompt-to-merge (option B).** When sign-in with a new provider's email matches a different existing OpenChat user's identifier, show a screen:

  'It looks like you may already have an OpenChat account associated with <email>.
   Would you like to merge them, or keep them separate?'
  [ Merge accounts ]  [ Keep separate ]

Matches Slack / Discord / GitHub conventions. User explicitly consents. Avoids the data-conflict footguns of auto-merge.

Implementation details:
- Detection: after auth provider verifies the new sign-in, server checks if its email matches an Identifier on a different User. If yes, fork to merge UX. If no, proceed with normal AuthMethod link to current user.
- Merge flow: server emits both User IDs to client; client shows merge confirmation modal with preview of conflicts (e.g. 'You have two display names: Jacob Cole and J. Cole. Which do you want to keep?'). User picks per-field. Server runs the merge atomically.
- Keep-separate flow: the new sign-in creates / signs into the OTHER account (not the current one). User ends up logged into whichever account they tapped 'Keep separate' from.
- Edge case: if BOTH accounts have AuthMethods (they're both established), we still ALLOW merge but require Magic Link or OTP confirmation from BOTH owning email addresses to prevent account theft via lapsed-credential attacks.

title: Manual identifier addition — add emails, phones, etc. for discovery after signup
description:
## What

Let users attach MORE identifiers (additional email addresses, additional phone numbers, eventually other handle types) to their account after signup — for the purpose of discovery, not auth.

Example: Jacob signs up via Apple with apple-relay email. Later he adds his real email 'jacob@ideapad.io' to his profile so people who have his email can find him on OpenChat. He doesn't necessarily want to sign in via that email — just be findable by it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Settings → Account → 'Discoverability identifiers' lists current bound identifiers (phone, emails)
- [ ] 'Add an email' / 'Add a phone' affordances; verify ownership via OTP (phone) or magic link (email)
- [ ] Each identifier has independent searchability toggle (links to 3ag.6)
- [ ] Each identifier shows verification state (verified ✓ / pending)
- [ ] Unverified identifiers do NOT appear in discovery match results
- [ ] User can remove an identifier (with confirmation; warn if it's the last verified one — they'd be undiscoverable)
- [ ] Server: identifier verification ownership flow per type:
  - Email: magic link sent to address, click confirms
  - Phone: OTP via SMS (reuses 3ag.3 SMS infra)

## Architecture

Reuses the Identifier model from 3ag.1. Each identifier is independent of any AuthMethod. A user might have:
- AuthMethod: Apple (signed up this way)
- Identifier: phone (added later for discovery — searchable on)
- Identifier: email primary@gmail.com (auto-bound from Apple — searchable off)
- Identifier: email work@ideapad.io (added manually — searchable on)

## Depends on

OpenChat-3ag.1 (identifier model), OpenChat-3ag.4 (multi-auth framework — separates auth from identifier concepts)

title: Per-identifier searchability settings — independent toggle per phone/email, default ON
description:
## What

Each identifier a user has (phone, email, etc.) gets an independent 'others can find me by this' toggle. Default ON for any new identifier added. Settings UX shows them as a list with per-item switches.

This replaces the single global 'let others find me' switch from 3ag.2's initial design. Granularity matters because users often want to be findable by their work email but NOT their personal cell phone, or vice versa.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each Identifier row has `isSearchable: boolean` (default true on creation)
- [ ] Settings UI: 'Discoverability' section shows each identifier with a toggle
- [ ] Per-identifier toggle UI shows:
  - identifier value (masked email like 'j••••@idea.io', phone like '+1 (•••) •••-1234' to avoid showing sensitive info to over-shoulder onlookers)
  - verified state
  - searchable toggle
  - 'Remove' affordance
- [ ] Server-side: discovery match (OpenChat-3ag.2) ONLY returns matches where the identifier's isSearchable is true
- [ ] Toggling to off does NOT delete the identifier; it just hides it from match results
- [ ] If user disables searchability on ALL identifiers, warn 'others won't be able to find you by phone or email — you can still be added via QR code or group invite'

## Default policy decisions

- Default ON for any new identifier (per Jacob): maximizes discovery utility
- 'Make me invisible to discovery entirely' is reachable by flipping each toggle off, OR via a master 'pause discovery' switch (defer to v2)

## Depends on

OpenChat-3ag.1 (identifier model)
OpenChat-3ag.2 (discovery matching code — needs to filter by isSearchable)

title: [DEFERRED — future] Passkey / WebAuthn login as a multi-auth provider
description:
## Why DEFERRED

Listed in the epic so the multi-auth architecture (3ag.4) accommodates it from day 1. No MVP commitment. Revisit once 3ag.4 lands and passkey UX has matured across Jacob's target user base (iOS 16+ widely adopted, Chrome desktop passkey UX stable).

## What

Add 'Sign in with passkey' as another AuthMethod provider type. User can register a passkey credential against their account (FaceID / TouchID / Windows Hello / hardware key). Subsequent logins use that credential — no password, no SMS, no OAuth roundtrip.

## Architecture sketch

- AuthMethod with provider='passkey', providerSubject=credentialId
- Server stores: credentialId, publicKey, transports (USB / NFC / internal), createdAt, lastUsedAt
- Sign-in: client → POST /api/auth/passkey/challenge → server returns challenge → client signs via navigator.credentials.get() → POST /api/auth/passkey/verify → server validates signature against stored publicKey → returns JWT
- Registration: similar flow with navigator.credentials.create()

## Why not now

- Passkey UX is still uneven across platforms (especially Android < 14)
- iOS shared keychain quirks complicate cross-device sync expectations
- Bigger wins are 3ag.1-3ag.6 first

## Revisit when

- iOS 17+ is 90% of the user base
- Apple/Google passkey sync (iCloud Keychain, Google Password Manager) is fully reliable
- After 3ag.4 ships so the integration is straightforward

title: Friends-only phone visibility option (experimental, future)
description:
## Why DEFERRED

Jacob 2026-06-03: 'Let's make a ticket to consider doing a friends-only thing for the future and play with that later.'

The 3ag.1 decision locked in 'hidden by default' for phone visibility — the most private default. This ticket holds the future-experiment idea of an intermediate tier: users could optionally make their phone visible to people they've already chatted with (or share a group with), without making it public.

## What

A user setting: 'Show my phone number to:'
- (default) Nobody — current 3ag.1 behavior
- People I've chatted with — new option
- (future) People I follow / friends list — when that concept exists

## When to revisit

After:
- 3ag.1, 3ag.2, 3ag.6 ship (the core identity layer)
- Real user feedback indicates demand for sharing phone with known contacts
- 'Friends' or 'follows' concept exists in the product

## Open questions for that future work

- Does 'people I've chatted with' include groups, or only 1:1 DMs?
- Is the visibility reciprocal (you see theirs only if they see yours)?
- Does removing someone from your contacts revoke their visibility into your phone?

Tickets it relates to: OpenChat-3ag.1 (visibility default), OpenChat-3ag.6 (per-identifier searchability)

title: Revisit discovery hash salt strategy — consider per-session or non-fixed salt
description:
## Why DEFERRED

Jacob 2026-06-03: 'For now we can just do A and make a ticket to consider a different salt later.'

3ag.2 ships with a fixed baked-in salt for simplicity. This ticket holds the future re-evaluation of whether to switch to per-session server-issued salts, ephemeral OAuth-style nonces, or some other stronger-against-rainbow-tables design.

## When to revisit

Triggers that should reopen this:
- User base grows past ~50k (enough that an attack rainbow table starts to be economically interesting to someone)
- We expose any kind of public-facing discovery API (not just in-app)
- Someone publishes a documented attack on fixed-salt discovery hashing
- Privacy / security audit recommends it (e.g. before any EU-wide launch where GDPR enforcement is active)
- A breach exposes user phones / emails — the fixed-salt scheme means anyone with that data + the salt can confirm matches against the user database

## Options to weigh when revisiting

1. **Per-session server-issued salt** — client requests salt at match start, server tracks issued salts, expires after N hours. Adds round-trip + state.
2. **Per-server-public-key Diffie-Hellman PSI** — proper private set intersection. Heaviest crypto but strongest privacy. Signal moved here.
3. **Bloom filter + private equality test** — Apple's CSAM-detection style approach. Strong but complex.

## Reference

- Signal's contact discovery history: https://signal.org/blog/private-contact-discovery/
- Apple Private Set Intersection paper if relevant

Related: OpenChat-3ag.2

description:
Five design questions still unresolved after the 2026-05-30 design conversation. See ~/code/openchat/docs/thoughts-design.md for full context.

title: Thoughts tab: 'open items only' filter chip (status=open / in-progress)
description:
## Why

User story (Jacob, 2026-06-02): "For any agent conversation or human chat thread, having a persistent view of just the *open* items — unresolved questions, pending decisions, incomplete threads — not the full history, just what's still live. Like a 'what's still hanging' panel. This is a key use case for OpenChat and a core value prop: ambient awareness of what's unresolved, not just a firehose of everything that happened."

## State of the design

The architecture for this **already exists** in `docs/thoughts-design.md` — Decision D1 (resolved 2026-05-30): *"One stream + filter chip. Open commitments / reminders render inline with a status pill. No separate Work tab."*

API surface is already specified: `GET /api/thoughts?kind=commitment&status=open` (line 224 of the design doc).

Status values per D10: `done`, `not-done`, `in-progress`, `acknowledged`, or `null`. Kinds that can carry status: fact, decision, commitment, reminder, observation, note.

## What this ticket is for

The base Thoughts tab shipped (OpenChat-3kr.1). The **filter chip UI** that makes the 'only open items' view discoverable to users has NOT been built as a standalone deliverable yet. This ticket is that delivery.

## Acceptance criteria

- Thoughts tab has a chip/segment toggle: 'All' / 'Open' / 'Done' (minimum).
- 'Open' = items with `status IN (open, in-progress, null-for-statusable-kinds)`. Acknowledged & done are hidden.
- Toggle state persists across app launches (per-user preference).
- Performance: rendering the filter doesn't trigger a full refetch — client-side filter on the already-loaded feed.
- Works on iOS, Android, /m/ web, /d/ web.

## Out of scope (separate tickets)

- Cross-conversation 'open items dashboard' that pulls open items from multiple chats into one view — this is a richer feature; OpenChat-3kr.4 ('Beads + memories surface inside OpenChat') is adjacent.
- Status-change UI (marking an open item done) — separate from this read-side filter.

## Notes

- Source idea also captured in Notestream as #idea #openchat (2026-06-02).
- Parent epic: OpenChat-3kr (thought-stream tab + agentic + NVC).

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
GEMINI SECOND OPINION + CODEX INDEPENDENT REVIEW (both 2026-06-01)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Saved at ~/memory/research/2026-06-01-gemini-openchat-desktop-fold-review.md
       and ~/memory/research/2026-06-01-codex-openchat-d-fold-review.md

REVISED APPROACH (Gemini + Codex):

═══ STRUCTURAL ═══

1. **Screen-level responsive routing (Gemini) — NOT top-level shell swap.**
   ❌ Original: return isDesktop ? <DesktopShell /> : <MobileShell /> in App.tsx → would unmount NavigationContainer, lose nav state + composer text + scroll + navigationRef.
   ✅ Fix: ONE NavigationContainer. Responsive swap inside individual SCREENS.

2. **Preserve main's bottom-tab architecture (Codex).**
   Main's current shape: RootStack → AuthedTabs → ChatsNavigator → ThoughtsNavigator.
   Desktop branch is from BEFORE this nested-tab refactor — porting requires implementing the responsive swap INSIDE the bottom-tab structure, not replacing it.
   ✅ In App.tsx: keep RootStack, AuthedTabs, ChatsNavigator, ThoughtsNavigator.
   ✅ Change only ChatsNavigator stack: ConversationsScreen → HomeScreen, ChatScreen → ChatScreenRouter.

3. **Use .web.tsx file extensions (Gemini) — NOT Platform.OS gates with React.lazy.**
   Metro compile-time resolves → 0 KB native bundle bloat.

4. **CRITICAL: every .web.tsx imported by shared code MUST have a native shim (Codex).**
   If App.tsx imports HomeScreen and only HomeScreen.web.tsx exists, iOS build fails.
   Required FILE PAIRS:
   - src/screens/HomeScreen.tsx (native: re-export ConversationsScreen)
   - src/screens/HomeScreen.web.tsx (responsive: useIsDesktop() → MasterDetailLayout vs ConversationsScreen)
   - src/screens/ChatScreenRouter.tsx (native: re-export ChatScreen)
   - src/screens/ChatScreenRouter.web.tsx (responsive: master-detail aware)
   - src/components/MasterDetailLayout.web.tsx (web-only, imported only from .web.tsx)
   - src/components/ChatPane.web.tsx (web-only)
   - src/components/ConversationList.web.tsx (web-only)
   - src/components/MaxWidthContent.web.tsx (web-only, narrow CSS-only impact)
   - src/screens/KeyboardShortcutsScreen.web.tsx (web-only, imported only by .web.tsx)
   - src/theme/breakpoints.ts (shared hook useIsDesktop)

5. **app.config.js for env-driven baseUrl, GUARDED for web only (Gemini).**
   const baseUrl = process.env.OPENCHAT_BASE_URL || undefined;
   experiments: { baseUrl: process.env.IS_WEB_BUILD ? baseUrl : undefined }
   Setting baseUrl on iOS / Android corrupts deep links + asset mapping.

6. **Breakpoint: 900px** (Gemini, confirmed).

═══ DEPLOY PIPELINE (Codex) ═══

7. **CRITICAL: distinct output dirs + inline env per command — NO leakage.**
   IS_WEB_BUILD=1 OPENCHAT_BASE_URL=/m npx expo export --platform web --output-dir dist-web-m --clear
   IS_WEB_BUILD=1 OPENCHAT_BASE_URL=/d npx expo export --platform web --output-dir dist-web-d --clear
   Then copy dist-web-m/ → client-mobile/dist/, dist-web-d/ → client-mobile-desktop/dist/.
   Add validator: grep '/m/' in client-mobile/dist/index.html (must hit), grep '/d/' must MISS. And vice versa for desktop. Fail deploy if cross-contamination.

═══ MERGE TIMING (Codex) ═══

8. **DO NOT MERGE TO main DURING TestFlight train.**
   Build 36 (v0.1.4) is currently in EAS auto-submit. 601 touches app.config.js, navigation/types.ts, route mappings, and several screens. Native EAS builds from main could break mid-train.
   - Work on a separate branch + worktree (~/.omnara/worktrees/openchat-mobile/<name>) NOW
   - WAIT until build 36 is visible in TestFlight
   - Pause new automatic native builds during the transition
   - After 601 lands, run ONE deliberate native EAS build as build 37 to verify

═══ ROOT CAUSE OF /d/ MESSAGE-HISTORY BUG (Gemini, verified) ═══

- desktop-ChatContext.tsx (lines 343-347): api.getMessages(id).then(msgs => setMessages(msgs))
- main-ChatContext.tsx (lines 527-531): api.getMessages(id).then(({ messages: msgs, hasMore }) => { setMessages(msgs); setHasMoreMessages(hasMore); })
- Main introduced pagination (OpenChat-vjc) that changed the API response shape from raw array to { messages, hasMore }. Desktop still expects array → setMessages(non-array) → 'prev.some is not a function' or empty render.
- Folding /d/ to main code automatically fixes this. NO manual patch needed.

title: Production Neo4j search error: 'Queries cannot be run directly on a session with an open transaction'
description:
## Symptom

Recurring error in openchat_app docker container logs on noos-prod (observed 2026-06-03 during SIWA debug):

```
Error performing search: Neo4jError: Queries cannot be run directly on a session with an open transaction; either run from within the transaction or use a different session.
  constructor: [Function: Neo4jError] { isRetriable: [Function (anonymous)] },
  gqlStatusDescription: 'error: general processing exception - unexpected error.
  Queries cannot be run directly on a session with an open transaction; either
  run from within the transaction or use a different session.',
```

Appeared multiple times consecutively, all from search operations.

## Root cause hypothesis

Somewhere in the search code path, a Neo4j driver session is having .run() called on it while a transaction is already open on the same session. Neo4j driver throws this immediately. Likely patterns to look for:

- A search handler that opens a transaction via session.beginTransaction(), then calls session.run() directly instead of tx.run() inside the transaction
- A reused session across multiple concurrent requests where one request's transaction is still open when another request tries to .run() on the same session
- Stale session reuse from a pooling layer

## Where to look

- src/routes/search.ts (or wherever search is defined — grep for 'search' in routes/)
- src/services/search.ts
- src/db.ts (driver + session factory)
- Any context provider that holds a long-lived session

## Acceptance

- [ ] Identify the actual code path triggering the error
- [ ] Fix by either (a) using session.run() outside any transaction (drop the explicit tx) OR (b) using tx.run() inside the transaction, depending on what the code is trying to do
- [ ] Add a regression test if reasonable
- [ ] Verify error disappears from production logs after deploy

## Impact

Search likely returns no results (or errors) for affected requests. Users may experience flaky search — sometimes works, sometimes silently fails. Worth investigating now since it's already in production.

## Related

- bd memory: proactive-error-monitoring-after-deploy (general pattern)

title: [P1] Self-serve agent API keys — seamless 'connect your bot' onboarding
description:
Make it dead simple for anyone (Jacob, a user, a friend) to plug their own agent/bot into OpenChat. Today picortex uses a one-off out-of-band JWT minted by a developer. We need a self-serve API key flow with re-viewable keys (NOT one-time-view), provenance fields, scopes, and a working MCP surface.

GOOD PRACTICES TO INHERIT FROM world-issue-tracker + wikihub:

1. **Prefix convention**: keys start with 'oc_' (parallels 'wh_' / 'wit_'). First 12 chars are the visible 'key prefix' used for UI display, full key only visible when retrieved.
2. **Standard Bearer auth**: 'Authorization: Bearer oc_…' on every endpoint, not a custom X-Agent-Key header. Matches WikiHub convention (cleaner than WIT's X-Agent-Key).
3. **Provenance fields**: each key has agent_name (e.g. 'my-summary-bot') + agent_version + scopes + expires_at + last_used_at — same shape as WikiHub's ApiKey model.
4. **Scopes**: at minimum 'read' + 'write'. Future: per-conversation scoping, send-only, read-only mention listening.
5. **Credentials file convention**: agents should expect to read from ~/.openchat/credentials.json (mode 0600), parallel to ~/.wikihub/credentials.json.
6. **MCP server**: build a sibling openchat-mcp-server adapter (parallel to wikihub's mcp-server/). Tools: oc_send_message, oc_list_conversations, oc_get_messages, oc_react, oc_create_dm, oc_register_agent. Exposes both stdio + HTTP transports.

DEVIATIONS FROM WIT/WikiHub (per Jacob's explicit feedback):

7. **Keys are RE-VIEWABLE, not one-time-view**. WIT + WikiHub both show the key once at creation and store only the hash — Jacob explicitly does NOT want that. Implementation: store the FULL plaintext key in DB, encrypted at rest with a server-side KMS key (OC_KEY_ENCRYPTION_SECRET env var, rotatable separately from the database). User can re-view any of their keys from Settings → Agent Keys at any time. Threat model: DB read leaks encryption-key-encrypted blob, not plaintext.

UI:
- Settings → Agent Keys (new section)
- List existing keys: name, prefix (oc_xxxx…), last used, expiry, [View] [Revoke] buttons
- 'New key' button: prompts for name + scopes + optional expiry → returns the full key, copy-to-clipboard
- Each key row has [View full key] → reveals plaintext after Face ID / passphrase re-auth (TBD)
- Each key row has [Copy] for the agent name + key in one shot

SERVER:
- New Neo4j node: :AgentKey { id, ownerUserId, name, keyPrefix, keyEncrypted, scopes, agentName, agentVersion, expiresAt, createdAt, lastUsedAt, revokedAt }
- (User)-[:OWNS_KEY]->(AgentKey)
- POST /api/agent-keys { name, scopes?, expiresAt? } — authed; mints + returns plaintext
- GET /api/agent-keys — authed; lists keys with prefix-only (no plaintext)
- GET /api/agent-keys/:id/reveal — authed; returns full plaintext key (with audit log entry)
- PATCH /api/agent-keys/:id { name?, scopes? } — authed; rename or change scope
- DELETE /api/agent-keys/:id — authed; sets revokedAt
- New middleware resolveActor: tries JWT first, then Bearer oc_… key. Resolves to owning user. Updates lastUsedAt async.
- Picortex's JWT-based auth stays (don't break) but is grandfathered; future bots go through this.

DOCS:
- README section: 'Connect your bot in 30 seconds'
  1. Settings → Agent Keys → Create
  2. curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer oc_…' https://chat.globalbr.ai/api/chat/conversations
- openchat-mcp-server README + Cursor/Claude Desktop config snippet
- Add to landing page /about: a 'Connect your bot' link with the 30-second walkthrough

ACCEPTANCE:
- A non-technical user can sign up, get an API key, and POST a message via curl in under 2 minutes
- An MCP-aware client (Claude Desktop) can be configured with one JSON snippet to talk to OpenChat
- Keys are re-viewable from Settings indefinitely (until revoked)
- Revocation is immediate (cached resolver invalidated within 60s)
- Audit log of key reveal events

- /Users/jacobcole/code/world-issue-tracker/supabase/functions/register-agent/index.ts (mint flow)
- /Users/jacobcole/code/wikihub/docs/MCP_CONNECTOR_BLUEPRINT.md (MCP server shape + tool surface)
- /Users/jacobcole/code/wikihub/mcp-server/ (working impl reference)
- /Users/jacobcole/code/picortex (current OpenChat bot for shape parity)

title: Promote 'Link an agent' to the top of Settings (one-tap agent-account binding)
description:
## What

Move the 'Agent Keys' / 'Link an agent' affordance to a prominent slot near the top of Settings (or even on the home screen as a banner during onboarding). Currently it's buried in the Settings menu and most users won't find it.

The goal: a new user opens OpenChat, immediately sees 'Want an AI assistant that can act on your behalf in chats? Link an agent.' One tap → mint an agent key with full account scope by default → copy snippet → paste into Claude / Codex / Cursor / etc. The agent then has full account control via MCP / API.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Settings screen: 'Connect an Agent' (or similar) is the FIRST or SECOND row, above Notifications / Account / etc.
- [ ] Tap → leads to a flow that:
  1. Explains in plain language what an agent is and what permissions it'll have
  2. Mints an agent key with default scope = 'full account' (read/write everything)
  3. Shows the key (re-revealable, AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest — already implemented)
  4. Provides copy-paste-ready snippets for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, etc.
- [ ] (Optional v2) Onboarding flow nudge — when a new user finishes signup, a soft prompt: 'Want to skip to having an AI handle your chats? [Link agent] [Maybe later]'
- [ ] Scope selector for advanced users — let them mint narrower-scope keys (e.g. read-only, or just for a single group). Default to full scope for the prominent flow because that's what most users want.

## Related

- The existing Agent Keys infra (per-user API keys, re-viewable, AES-256-GCM at rest, via Settings → Agent Keys per the original product description)
- OpenChat-3kr.3 (Agentic features — summon-an-agent UI) — overlaps
- Above ticket (group chat agent sharing) — a complementary affordance: this links an agent at the account level, that one shares an agent at the group level

## Open

- Should the agent have a visible 'persona' in the user's other chats? E.g. when the agent sends a message on behalf of the user, is it tagged as such? Defer to v2 — for v1 the agent acts AS the user, no tag.
- Should there be a 'pause my agent' kill switch on the home screen? Probably yes — file as a follow-up.

title: Reconnecting bar: goes behind notch + needs standard location
description:
## Symptom

Jacob report 2026-06-03: 'the off-line reconnecting bar is very strange it goes behind the notch and also let's make sure we put it in a standard location.'

The connection-status indicator (shown when websocket/network is reconnecting) is rendering behind the iPhone notch / Dynamic Island instead of respecting the safe area. Visible to every user, every time their network blips — high-visibility bug.

## Likely surfaces

- src/components/ — look for ConnectionStatusBar / NetworkStatusBanner / ReconnectingBanner / OfflineBar / similar
- src/contexts/SocketContext or wherever the socket state is exposed
- Whatever overlay component renders during socket reconnect

## Acceptance

- [ ] Bar respects iPhone notch / Dynamic Island safe area (uses useSafeAreaInsets() or SafeAreaView)
- [ ] Bar in a 'standard location' — either:
  - **(a) below the nav header**, full-width thin strip (iOS pattern — matches Messages, WhatsApp)
  - **(b) at the very top in the status-bar slot**, replacing notification spacing momentarily (Twitter/X pattern)
  - Pick one and apply consistently. Recommend (a) — more discoverable + doesn't fight with the status bar
- [ ] Same fix on Android (Dynamic Island doesn't apply but navbar safe-area still matters)
- [ ] Same fix on web — should NOT use safe-area there, but should be in the same visual slot relative to the nav
- [ ] Bar dismisses smoothly on reconnect (fade or slide out, not pop)
- [ ] Bar text is readable in both light/dark mode
- [ ] Tap target on the bar (if any) is ≥ 44pt

title: Threaded replies (Slack-style) — collapse-able threads off any message
description:
## Why DEFERRED (design ticket for the future)

Jacob 2026-06-03: "Let's also add a design ticket for the future to support replies with threading like Slack so you can really collapse the threads."

OpenChat currently supports reply-as-quote (one message points back at another). This ticket is the LARGER design: full Slack/Discord-style threading where each message can spawn a sub-conversation that appears collapsed in the main channel and expanded in a side panel or inline-expanded view.

Distinct from existing replies — this is structural threading, not quote-citation.

## What

- Any message can spawn a thread. Tap the message, "Reply in thread", opens a thread view that's a sub-conversation rooted at that parent message.
- In the main channel, the parent message shows an "X replies, last reply Yh ago" affordance under it. Tap to expand the thread inline (or open in a side panel on tablet/web).
- Thread replies are NOT visible in the main channel feed by default. Users can opt in to "show replies in channel" as a setting.
- Threads can be followed independently — notify me of replies even if I'm not following the channel.
- @-mentions in a thread notify the mentioned user even if they weren't following the thread.

## Open design questions

1. **Thread depth** — flat (single level, all replies attach to the parent) or nested (replies-to-replies form a tree). Slack does flat. Discord does flat. Twitter does nested. Recommend FLAT for v1 (simpler model, well-understood). Nested can be v2.

2. **History semantics in groups** — when someone joins a group later, do they see existing threads? Probably yes. When an agent joins (per OpenChat-yr2), do threads show in the agent's accessible message list? Yes for full history; for from-join-only mode, threads created after the join.

3. **Thread vs forward** — pulling a thread out into a new conversation is closer to forward. Keep them distinct in the UX. Threading stays in place; forwarding spawns a new conversation rooted at a copied message.

4. **Mobile UX** — Slack mobile opens threads in a full-screen view. OpenChat mobile probably does the same. Web/desktop can do inline OR side-panel; pick side-panel to match Slack's known pattern.

5. **Notification semantics** —
   - Reply in thread: notify thread participants + thread followers
   - @-mention in thread: also notify the mentioned user
   - Default for channel's regular members: NOT notified of thread replies they're not in
   - Slack's defaults sparked years of debate; design carefully

6. **Search** — threaded messages need to be findable in search. Index them as their own messages with a "thread root" attribute. UX: search result that's in a thread shows "In a thread from <parent>" so you can jump to the thread.

7. **Thoughts integration** — per OpenChat-3kr, hashtags inside thread replies should still extract to Thoughts. Thread replies are still messages.

8. **Agents in threads** (per OpenChat-yr2) — agents added to a group can reply in threads. Agents probably should default to thread-following "only when @-mentioned" to avoid noise. Configurable per agent.

## Schema sketch (Cypher-ish)

Relationship: Message-REPLY_OF-Message (current quote-reply, keep as-is)
New relationship: Message-THREAD_PARENT-Message (this message is a thread reply rooted at parent)
Denormalized properties on parent for UI: threadCount (int), lastReplyAt (datetime)

Alternative: threads as their own Conversation sub-type rooted at the parent message. Cleaner separation but bigger refactor. Decide at design time.

## When to revisit

- After OpenChat-yr2 (group-agent sharing) ships — agents-in-threads is the most interesting use case for threading and shapes design decisions
- After user feedback on the current quote-reply model surfaces — if users are clearly trying to thread already and finding the quote-reply too lightweight
- Before OpenChat hits a user count that makes single-stream group chats overwhelming

## Related

- OpenChat-yr2 (group chats with agents) — informs notification + history defaults
- OpenChat-3kr (Thoughts) — thread replies still count for hashtag extraction
- OpenChat-r1y (offline-send queue) — needs to handle thread replies the same as channel messages

description:
Sibling of picortex-hal (P2, picortex-side group-chat validation pass). Today picortex is only tested/used in DMs (type: 'direct') on chat.globalbr.ai. The bot auto-joins any conversation it's a participant in via polling GET /api/chat/conversations, but OpenChat may have different routing semantics for group vs direct conversations and there is no 'add bot to group' flow.

Scope
- Verify end-to-end: bot added as participant in a type='group' Conversation, message:new fires for bot on group messages, bot's message:send via socket broadcasts correctly to all group participants.
- Audit server/src/routes/chat.ts and server/src/websocket/chatHandler.ts for any branch that treats type='group' differently from type='direct' (permission checks, room membership, deduplication, etc.).
- Test scenarios: (a) bot in group from creation, (b) bot added to existing group after creation, (c) bot removed from group, (d) multiple humans + bot in same group, (e) bot-only messages vs human-to-human messages (discriminate/mention-only behavior).

Likely implementation gaps
- UI: no 'add bot to group' flow in the OpenChat web client (see OpenChat-88z new-conversation contact picker for nearby UX).
- Server: no participant:added socket event emitted when a user is added to an existing conversation — bot would miss it until next 30s poll (same race as the first-message bug, see sibling ticket 'First message to picortex gets no reply').

title: 401 cascade: app shows error toast then strands user, no logout/refresh path
description:
When the access token expires (15min from Noos), the SPA at chat.globalbr.ai is left in a broken state:

Repro (verified live with Chrome DevTools 2026-05-30, screenshots in /tmp/openchat-04-toast-broken-no-dismiss.png):
1. Token in localStorage.openchat_token expires
2. GET /api/chat/conversations returns 401
3. ApiClient.fetch (client/src/api.ts) throws 'Invalid or expired token' — no refresh attempt, no localStorage clear, no logout, no redirect
4. ChatContext.loadConversations catch shows toast.error('Failed to load conversations') — auto-dismisses after 6s, no X button, no way to dismiss manually
5. Socket.IO useChatSocket connect_error fires with server-side Error('Invalid token') — only console.errors, perpetual 'Reconnecting...' spinner
6. User is stranded on the chat page with stale UI, no way to recover without manually clearing localStorage

Fix work is in git stash@{0}: 'stash-during-darkmode-deploy' — 6 files, ~455 insertions, codex-reviewed shape + implementation. Includes:
- Single-flight refresh via shared promise (Noos refresh tokens are rotated — would race otherwise)
- New refreshAccessToken() / clearAuth() / emitTokenRefreshed / emitAuthExpired helpers in api.ts
- 401-then-refresh-then-retry in fetch<T>() and getMe() (also fixes latent /me URL bug — was hitting /api/chat/me instead of /api/auth/me)
- Refresh-loop guard: consecutiveRefreshes counter capped at REFRESH_LOOP_LIMIT=3 (codex 2026-05-30 caught the per-effect-run flag would loop forever if every refreshed token is rejected)
- ChatProvider listens for noos:token-refreshed (updates React token state) + noos:auth-expired (clears state + navigate('/login') + toast)
- New utils/toastError.tsx component: dismissible (X button + click-anywhere + Esc), role=alert, aria-live=assertive, stable-id de-dupe (so loadConversations spam doesn't stack)
- All 10 toast.error() sites swapped to toastError() with stable IDs
- logout() now clears openchat_refresh_token (was leaking)
- register/ssoExchange now persist refreshToken (was dropping it)

Codex critique status: blessed shape + impl after addressing the refresh-loop guard. Remaining concerns are non-blocking (SSR guards in ChatProvider, possible slight double-toast on auth-expired).

title: [mobile][bug] Chat scroll behavior: at-bottom-aware auto-scroll + new-messages pill
description:
Today: ChatScreen.tsx scrolls to bottom on EVERY message arrival, regardless of where the user is scrolled. If the user scrolled up to read history, a new message yanks them down. Real-chat-app expectation:

1. AT BOTTOM + new message arrives → smooth-scroll to keep them at the latest
2. SCROLLED UP + new message arrives → DON'T scroll. Show a floating 'N new messages ↓' pill above the composer
3. Tap pill → scroll to bottom + clear unread count
4. Reach bottom by manual scroll → clear unread count automatically
5. Own message sent → always scroll to bottom (the user is implicitly at-bottom)

Affects iOS app + RN-web /m/ + RN-web /d/. One implementation in src/screens/ChatScreen.tsx covers all three.

Pitfalls to handle correctly:
- Keyboard open/close shifts layout; ignore scroll events for ~200ms after keyboard transition OR snap to bottom if we WERE at bottom before keyboard opened
- Threshold for 'at bottom' should be ~50-100px (not 0) because RN scroll never hits exact bottom in practice
- Programmatic scrollToEnd() should still update isAtBottom correctly via onScroll
- Day separators jump contentSize between messages; use onContentSizeChange to recompute isAtBottom after content grows

Acceptance: tester sends 10 messages while scrolled up reading history; ChatScreen doesn't scroll them; pill shows '10 new messages ↓'; tapping pill scrolls to bottom + pill disappears.

title: register() and ssoExchange() drop refreshToken from the return — session is non-refreshable from birth
description:

title: [UX] Dark mode for OpenChat web app
description:
Add proper dark mode to OpenChat's web client. The app is currently bg-white / text-gray-900 across all surfaces — fine in daylight, harsh at night, and obviously not parity with the iMessage / WhatsApp / Telegram default that users expect.

## Approach
- Enable Tailwind dark mode: 'class' strategy in tailwind.config.js (not 'media' — we want user override, not system-only).
- Toggle in user menu (ChatSidebar's user dropdown): Light / Dark / System. Default 'System'.
- Persist choice in localStorage 'openchat_theme'. On boot, main.tsx applies the saved/derived class to <html>.
- React to system pref changes (matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').addEventListener) when in System mode.
- Update the existing <meta name='theme-color'> from #3b82f6 to also have a dark variant (use media-attribute form: <meta name='theme-color' content='#1e293b' media='(prefers-color-scheme: dark)'>) so the iOS Safari URL-bar tints correctly.
- Update manifest.webmanifest theme_color + background_color to have light/dark counterparts where browsers support it (only some do; safe to keep current light defaults).

## Files to audit for hardcoded colors
Every component that currently uses bg-white / bg-gray-50 / text-gray-* / border-gray-* needs dark: variants. Inventory from grep:
- client/src/pages/ChatPage.tsx (bg-gray-50 outer, header bg-white)
- client/src/components/ChatSidebar.tsx (bg-white, gray borders, status dropdown)
- client/src/components/ConversationList.tsx
- client/src/components/MessageList.tsx (bg-blue-500 own bubbles -> stays; bg-gray-100 other bubbles -> dark:bg-gray-700; text-gray-900 -> dark:text-gray-100)
- client/src/components/MessageInput.tsx (bg-white form, border-gray-200, border-gray-300 input)
- client/src/components/GroupSettings.tsx (modal bg-white)
- client/src/components/PresenceIndicator.tsx (presence dot colors — likely keep)
- client/src/components/InstallPrompt.tsx (sheet bg-white)
- client/src/App.tsx Toaster (already uses bg-red-100 / bg-green-100 — those work in both modes but darker variants would be cleaner)
- client/src/index.css base body bg
- The Noos feedback widget is 3rd-party; can't directly themed. data-theme='auto' is already set in index.html so it should respect prefers-color-scheme automatically.

## UX details
- Switch should be near-instant (no flash of unstyled content). Apply theme class BEFORE React mounts — in a small inline <script> in index.html that reads localStorage and applies the class to <html> synchronously.
- Bubble color choice for dark mode: own messages stay blue, others go to dark-gray (e.g. bg-slate-700). Sender-name labels go to slate-400.
- Status indicators (green/yellow/red/gray dots) stay the same vivid colors in both modes.
- Floating Noos widget data-theme='auto' should pick up the change.

## Acceptance
- Toggle in user menu works (Light / Dark / System).
- System mode tracks OS preference live (no reload needed).
- No flash of light theme on dark-mode-saved cold load.
- All conversation surfaces (list / chat / group settings modal / install prompt / login) look polished in dark.
- iOS Safari URL-bar tints with the theme.

## Phase
Phase 1 polish — chunky-but-not-blocking. Ship before declaring mobile UX 'done.' Roughly half a day of careful component-by-component audit + a couple of hours for the theme toggle infrastructure.

The screen has <KeyboardAvoidingView behavior={Platform.OS === 'ios' ? 'padding' : undefined}> with keyboardVerticalOffset={Platform.OS === 'ios' ? 90 : 0} in ChatScreen.tsx. Repro: open any conversation on iPhone (TestFlight build 14), tap the text input. Observe composer is partly visible / partly hidden.

1. Switch to react-native-keyboard-controller (handles edge cases better than KeyboardAvoidingView; integrates with the native gesture handler)
2. Or: read useSafeAreaInsets + the header height (useHeaderHeight from react-navigation) at runtime and compute the offset dynamically instead of hardcoding 90
3. Or: behavior='height' instead of 'padding' on iOS

Acceptance: composer + send button fully visible above the keyboard on iPhone 13/14/15-class devices in both light/dark mode, with and without the tab bar visible.

description:
## Symptom (reported by Jacob 2026-06-03)

User-reported: "Sign up with Apple is broken and it actually weirdly goes off the bottom of the screen on my friends phone."

Two stacked issues to disambiguate:

1. **Layout bug**: Sign In with Apple UI extends past the bottom safe area on at least one iPhone model. Likely a missing SafeAreaView or a fixed height that doesn't account for the home indicator on Face-ID-era devices.
2. **Functional bug**: 'Broken' could mean the button itself, a downstream modal, or the post-Apple-callback flow that creates the OpenChat user.

## Information needed (asked Jacob; reply pending)

- [ ] Friend's iPhone model + iOS version
- [ ] Which UI element goes off-screen (button, modal, callback screen)
- [ ] Specific failure mode: tap-doesn't-work / modal-fails / account-doesn't-create
- [ ] Screenshot or screen recording

## Likely surfaces to inspect

- The Apple-signin button render in the onboarding flow
- expo-apple-authentication plugin config — is the button height fixed?
- The Noos SSO callback handler for Apple credential exchange
- Server-side: src/routes/auth.ts Apple flow (does it accept the credential? store the user?)

## Priority

P1 — this is a sign-up flow blocker for new external users (TestFlight F&F). If Apple sign-in is broken, the only sign-up paths are Google and email/password.

Last known working: ? (need to check when Apple sign-in last shipped or last got tested)

title: Decide canonical agent integration path: MCP/keys vs picortex vs openchat-agent
description:
Three different 'agent connects to OpenChat' paths exist. Pick one canonical
path going forward so the question doesn't get re-litigated.

Full discussion + timeline + proposed decision: docs/agent-integration-paths.md

## Three paths
| # | Path | Identity | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | picortex (GCP VM) | shared bot user picortex_bot_… | deployed |
| 2 | openchat-agent (~/code/openchat-agent) | shared bot user, slimmer rewrite | built 2026-05-31, never deployed |

1. openchat-mcp-server + agent keys = canonical recommended path.
2. picortex stays running with deprecation date 2026-09-01.

4. File new ticket if a 'listen in real time' use case appears later (probably a 'listen' scope on agent keys + WebSocket auth).

- Owner signs off on the proposal in docs/agent-integration-paths.md (or amends it)

title: Sync SSO flow with Thoughtstreams / latest Noos pattern
description:
OpenChat SSO diverges from Thoughtstreams:

1. Thoughtstreams proxies /api/auth/sso-exchange through its own server; OpenChat calls Noos directly from the browser (cross-origin, requires CORS, leaks Noos URL, bakes in VITE_NOOS_URL at build time). Refactor OpenChat to POST to /api/auth/sso-exchange on its own server and have the server talk to Noos internally via NOOS_API_URL (already in docker-compose). Benefits: no cross-origin fetch, no VITE_NOOS_URL dependency for the exchange path, matches Thoughtstreams.

2. Thoughtstreams calls /auth/session-check on load to auto-resume a Noos session. OpenChat does not — users must click Continue with Noos even if already signed in on ts.globalbr.ai. Add session-check for true cross-app SSO.

3. Consider extracting a shared noos-sso npm module (used by OpenChat, Thoughtstreams, thoughtstream-gemini-jacob) so auth drift stops happening per-app. Tracked under noos-sso-ecosystem epic.
close_reason:
Obviated 2026-06-01 by /legacy/ deprecation (OpenChat-ixd default decision: don't invest in /legacy):

PART 1 (Vite client → server-proxy SSO exchange): The cross-origin sso-exchange call lives only in client/src/api.ts (the legacy Vite client). Per ixd, /legacy/ is deprecated; we're not investing in its refactors.

PART 2 (cross-app session-check on load): Could benefit /m/ and /d/ users coming from globalbr.ai. But requires Noos server cooperation and is genuinely separate work — file a new ticket if/when this becomes a priority.

PART 3 (shared noos-sso npm module): Belongs to the noos-sso-ecosystem epic, not OpenChat-scoped.

MOBILE (the canonical client now) does NOT have this divergence — it uses Google OAuth + Apple SIWA directly, no SSO-exchange round-trip. Verified via grep of openchat-mobile/src/ — zero matches for sso-exchange.

title: Reply UX polish: composer doesn't auto-focus after tap-to-reply + visual distinction of replies is weak
description:
## Symptoms (Jacob 2026-06-03)

Two related subtleties in the existing quote-reply feature that make replies feel sloppy:

### A. Composer doesn't focus after tap-to-reply

When the user taps 'Reply' on a message (long-press menu or swipe action), the composer area shows the quoted-message pill, but the keyboard does NOT auto-show and the text input does NOT auto-focus. User has to manually tap into the composer to start typing.

Expected: tap reply → quoted pill appears → keyboard rises → cursor lands in the input → user starts typing immediately. This is what Messages, WhatsApp, Slack, Discord all do.

### B. Visual distinction between replies and non-replies is weak

In the message list, a reply message renders similarly to a non-reply. The quoted-parent reference is shown but doesn't read as 'this message is a REPLY to that' at a glance. Users have to look closely to tell which messages are replies.

Expected: stronger visual treatment — a vertical accent line connecting the reply to its quoted source, indented body, or a clearer 'replying to <name>:' header. Pick a pattern from Slack/Messages/Discord that matches the existing design language.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After tapping reply on a message:
  - Composer becomes focused (TextInput.focus() called)
  - Keyboard rises on mobile
  - Quoted-message pill is visible above the input
  - The cursor is in the input ready to type
  - Tested on iOS + Android
- [ ] Reply messages in the list have clearly stronger visual treatment than non-reply messages, such as:
  - Vertical accent stripe (1-2px wide cobalt or muted color) on the left of the reply bubble extending up to the quoted message
  - OR an indented bubble that visually nests under the quoted message
  - OR a clear 'replying to <name>:' caption above the reply text
  - Pick one pattern that fits the existing design + apply consistently
- [ ] Both fixes preserve all existing behavior (long-press menu still works, swipe-to-reply still works, sending the reply still attaches the right parent message ID)

## Surfaces likely to touch

- src/screens/ChatScreen.tsx — composer focus + ref management
- src/components/MessageBubble (or whatever renders messages) — visual treatment for reply messages
- src/components/MessageComposer / ReplyPill — the quoted-message pill above the input
- Possibly a context that tracks the in-progress reply target

## Out of scope (separate work)

- Full Slack-style threading (filed as OpenChat-ao8, deferred)
- Editing the visual treatment of the parent message being replied to
- Notification or push semantics around replies
close_reason: Fixed in branch fix/openchat-imt-reply-ux-polish (~/code/openchat-mobile). Fix A: composer auto-focus via setTimeout 80ms in handleReply (reuses NVC-modal-close pattern). Fix B: 3px vertical accent stripe — left/cobalt on others' bubbles, right/white-55% on own bubbles, suppressed on error state. Caveat: 3px border adds 3px to bubble layout box — visually imperceptible, but flagged in case padding compensation is wanted. ChatPane.web.tsx doesn't exist; ChatScreenRouter.web.tsx routes through the same ChatScreen so web is covered.

title: [decision] Keep classical Vite web client alive for WIT / SDK embed scenarios?
description:
Future consideration raised 2026-06-01: if we want to embed OpenChat directly into worldissuetracker.com (or any other product), should we maintain the classical Vite web client at /legacy/ as the embed substrate?

═══ DEFAULT DECISION (Codex review 2026-06-01) ═══

**Do NOT invest in /legacy. Future embed is a separate minimal SDK built when WIT has a real spec.**

Reasoning:
- /legacy already deprecated; keeping it alive repeats the branch/client drift problem OpenChat-601 is trying to kill
- /m iframe is too heavy and too app-shaped for an SDK
- A minimal embed should be purpose-built around REST/socket APIs and a narrow product contract — not the broad chat-app shell
- Adding /legacy maintenance now is the same anti-pattern that caused OpenChat-601

═══ REVISIT TRIGGERS ═══

- WIT product spec for embedded chat exists
- Another product (other than WIT) requests an embed
- We measure bundle sizes and find /m/ embeddable as iframe is acceptable for WIT's use case

═══ ACTION (FOR NOW) ═══

- Hold the question, document the default
- Do NOT keep /legacy alive specifically for embed
- After OpenChat-601 lands, re-evaluate with measured data: bundle sizes, WIT product needs
- Status: held open as a decision marker, not as work

Original options considered:
A. Embed /m/ as iframe — heavy bundle, but zero new code
B. Maintain Vite client — REJECTED, double-write maintenance tax

- After: cannot sign back in with same email (or: re-signup creates a new fresh account)
