title: Onboarding for non-app QR scans: HTTPS-only QRs + server-rendered intent landing pages
description:
USER ASK (2026-06-02): when someone scans a QR (per-user add or group invite) and they don't have the app installed or even TestFlight, the flow breaks down. What SHOULD happen vs what does happen today:

═══ TODAY ═══
- Homepage QR: https://chat.globalbr.ai/ → Safari opens landing page (works)
- Per-user QR (MyQrCodeScreen): openchat://user/<id>?v=1 → Safari shows 'Cannot open URL' (BROKEN for non-installed users; works only when app is installed)
- Group invite QR: https://chat.globalbr.ai/i/<token> → Safari opens legacy SPA → forces sign-in (legacy lacks 84u.1 intent stash) → intent lost after OAuth bounce

═══ PROPOSED ═══
Phase 1 (this ticket):
- Change MyQrCodeScreen to encode HTTPS: https://chat.globalbr.ai/u/<userId>
- Add server-side GET /u/:userId that renders a clean SSR page (no JS required) showing:
  * '@<name> wants to add you on OpenChat'
  * Their avatar (initials if no photo)
  * 3 CTAs: 'Open in OpenChat app' (universal link, falls through to web on no-app) | 'Sign up + add them on mobile web' (/m/?intent=add-user&id=<id>) | 'Get the iOS app' (TestFlight link with the intent passed via Apple universal link metadata)
  * Each CTA preserves the intent so post-sign-in lands on ContactProfile

Phase 2 (84u.2 dependency):
- Once Associated Domains capability lands (OpenChat-84u.2), HTTPS links open the app directly on installed devices. The SSR landing page becomes the no-app fallback only.

Phase 3 (out of scope here):
- Group invite SSR landing page (parallel design — 'You've been invited to join <group>')
- Cross-device intent handoff (scan on phone, sign in on desktop, intent still resolves)

═══ KEY DESIGN PRINCIPLES ═══
1. The QR should ALWAYS work in any iOS scanner. No 'openchat://' scheme-only QRs.
2. Server-side render the intent page — works without JS, works without sign-in.
3. Carry intent across OAuth: ?intent=add-user&id=<id> survives the Google round-trip via sessionStorage (already shipped in 84u.1 for /m/).
4. Show value BEFORE asking for sign-up — user sees 'Sandeep wants to add you' before being asked to create an account. Cuts onboarding friction.

═══ ACCEPTANCE ═══
- [ ] MyQrCodeScreen encodes https URL
- [ ] GET /u/:userId server route serves SSR landing with user name + 3 install CTAs
- [ ] /m/?intent=add-user&id=<id> stashes intent, resumes after sign-in to ContactProfile
- [ ] Non-installed iPhone user can scan + sign-up + land on add-contact in <60s
- [ ] No JS required for the SSR page to render basic content

title: Reconsider openchat-agent: shared-bot use case is distinct from MCP, not redundant
description:
Pulling this back out of 'archive' (OpenChat-do2) for reconsideration. OpenChat-fwi recommended archiving openchat-agent on the premise that openchat-mcp-server replaces it. That's wrong — they serve different use cases.

## What openchat-agent actually is
Headless Node service, ~300 LOC. NOT a cloud box. NOT a VM. Just code. Designed to ship as a systemd unit (`/opt/openchat-agent/`) or docker container, runs on any Linux host. Never deployed. Reuses (or replaces) picortex's bot JWT.

## Two distinct use cases — both legitimate
| Use case | Best path |
|---|---|
| 'MY agent reads MY chats' (single user, on-demand) | **MCP via per-user API key** |
| 'Shared assistant lives in our group, responds to @mentions, no per-user setup' | **openchat-agent (or picortex)** |

The MCP path requires every user to install Claude Desktop / Cursor / etc., mint a key, paste a config. Shared-bot path requires zero user setup — the bot just appears in the group and you @ it.

These are complementary, not competing.

## What needs to be answered
1. Do we want a shared OpenChat bot (vs. only per-user MCP)? If yes:
2. Should it be openchat-agent (slim, OpenChat-only) or keep picortex (already deployed)?
3. Where does it run? Options:
   - Co-host on picortex-v1 (cheap, defeats isolation)
   - testcortex (already there, but ⚠️ SECURITY — testcortex is on Tailscale; agent with shell-tool access could pivot — see ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md testcortex security section)
   - New GCP e2-micro ($5/mo, isolated)
   - Mac Mini (free, but Mac Mini has many other things)
   - Fly.io / Hetzner (cheap small VM)
4. Bot identity: keep picortex_bot or fresh user?
5. What about tools — should the shared bot have access to user-scoped operations? (probably not — least-privilege says shared bot can only do shared-conversation things)

## Decision needed before acting on OpenChat-do2
Until this ticket is resolved, DO NOT execute OpenChat-do2 (archive openchat-agent). If decision = 'no shared bot ever, MCP is enough', then OpenChat-do2 can proceed.

## Cross-references
- OpenChat-fwi (agent integration paths)
- OpenChat-do2 (archive openchat-agent — now BLOCKED on this)
- OpenChat-xem (picortex deprecation 2026-09-01 — may need adjustment if we keep the shared-bot path on openchat-agent)
- docs/agent-integration-paths.md (the design doc — needs an update reflecting this distinction)

title: Offline-send behavior: WhatsApp-style queue + sync (composer never blocks; messages flush when reconnected)
description:
USER ASK (2026-06-01): when offline, sending a message should behave like WhatsApp — the message appears in the composer immediately with a 'sending' state (or queue indicator), then automatically flushes to server when the socket reconnects. Today the composer's send button is disabled when offline (per OfflineBanner logic) or the message fails silently.

CURRENT STATE:
- OfflineBanner mounted globally (OpenChat-5ay shipped)
- ChatContext.isConnected drives the banner
- Messages send via api.sendMessage → if 401/500/network → caught by clientLogger but the user just sees a failure with no retry
- Optimistic UI: ChatScreen appends to local messages array BEFORE server confirms

DESIRED:
1. Composer always sends → message gets a clientId + 'pending' status
2. If offline, message stays 'pending' with a small ⏳ indicator (matches WhatsApp's clock icon)
3. On socket reconnect, replay all pending messages in send order
4. Server should accept idempotency via clientId to prevent duplicates on reconnect race
5. AsyncStorage persist the pending queue so app kill + reopen still delivers
6. Show 'sent' / 'delivered' / 'read' once server confirms (already shipped — OpenChat-0nj)

SCOPE:
- New client-side service: pendingMessageQueue.ts (enqueue, flushOnReconnect, persist to AsyncStorage)
- ChatContext.sendMessage: append to queue, attempt immediate send if online; queue otherwise
- Socket on('connect'): flush queue
- Server POST /messages: accept optional clientMessageId, dedupe via index

CAVEATS / FOLLOW-UPS:
- Voice messages and image attachments need queue serialization too (or a 'sending' state for them)
- Edit / delete of a still-pending message needs special-case (allow local mutation before flush)
- ChatScreen needs to show pending state distinctly from server-confirmed

ESTIMATED EFFORT: 3-4 hours (touches client + server + careful Cypher dedupe)

title: [Mobile] Dark mode for the React Native app (when it lands)
description:
When the React Native prototype (OpenChat-dv0) becomes a real shipping app, it needs dark mode parity with the web app.

## Approach
- React Native: useColorScheme() from 'react-native' (Appearance API) gives system preference live.
- Theme provider context (or just a useThemed hook) exposing semantic tokens (background, surface, primary, textPrimary, textSecondary, divider, bubbleOwn, bubbleOther, bubbleOwnText, bubbleOtherText, etc.).
- Persist user override (Light / Dark / System) via AsyncStorage / MMKV.
- All shared design tokens should match the web app's dark palette one-to-one so cross-platform users see the same colors.
- Native side benefits the web app can't easily get:
  - Status bar style (light/dark content) via StatusBar component.
  - iOS navigation bar tint (UIBarStyle / scheme on the wrapper).
  - Apple's smart-invert handled by the system.
  - Native blur effects on dark surfaces (BlurView) where appropriate.

## Cross-platform consistency
- Pick the design tokens BEFORE writing the web dark mode (OpenChat-?? sibling ticket). Web and RN should share a single color spec, not diverge.
- Document the spec in a single ~/code/openchat/docs/theme.md or similar.
- If we later add a Capacitor or full-RN shell, the same tokens apply.

## Phase
Phase 2 — does NOT need to land until the RN prototype itself does (OpenChat-dv0). Filed now so it's not forgotten when the RN work begins.

Depends on OpenChat-dv0 (RN prototype) + the web dark mode sibling ticket for the source-of-truth color spec.

title: Deploy openchat-agent on fresh GCP e2-micro (shared-bot canonical)
description:
Per OpenChat-p9y + Codex 2026-06-01 review: openchat-agent is the canonical shared-bot path. Deploy it on a fresh isolated GCP e2-micro.

## Why this host (not the alternatives)
- GCP e2-micro: ~$5/mo, fully isolated, legible security boundary
- NOT testcortex: it's on Jacob's Tailscale; agent capabilities tend to grow even if v1 has no shell tools — Codex's words. Boundary belongs before compromise, not after.
- NOT picortex-v1 co-host: defeats the isolation that justifies retiring picortex
- NOT Mac Mini: too many other services
- NOT Fly.io / Hetzner: GCP credits available; consistency with rest of fleet

## Steps
1. Reserve static IP: `gcloud compute addresses create openchat-agent-ip --region=us-central1`
2. Provision: `gcloud compute instances create openchat-agent --zone=us-central1-a --machine-type=e2-micro --image-family=ubuntu-2404-lts-amd64 --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud --boot-disk-size=20GB --address=openchat-agent-ip --tags=https-server`
3. Bootstrap: install node 20, scp openchat-agent source up, npm ci --omit=dev, install systemd unit per README
4. .env contents: OPENCHAT_BOT_JWT (reuse picortex's), OPENCHAT_BASE_URL=https://chat.globalbr.ai, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (fresh, not picortex's), BOT_NAME=picortex (or whatever — keep mention trigger working)
5. Start service, verify in OpenChat: @ the bot in a test group, expect a reply
6. Observe for 48h
7. Stop picortex's OpenChat participation (kill openchat side of dispatcher only; leave Linq side running on picortex-v1 for now)
8. Decommission picortex-v1 GCP VM ~2 weeks after green status on openchat-agent

## Decision needed before step 4
- Bot identity: keep `picortex_bot_7ecd2883dbd5ceef` (preserves message history) or fresh `openchat_assistant_…` user (clean slate)?
- Bot display name: 'picortex' (existing mention trigger) or rename to something OpenChat-native ('OpenChat AI', 'Echo', etc.)?

## Acceptance
- openchat-agent VM running, systemd service active
- @mention in a group → reply within 5s
- picortex-v1 OpenChat side stopped, no double-reply
- 1 week of observation, no crashes
- docs/agent-integration-paths.md updated with the actual deployed state

## Dependencies
- OpenChat-p9y (the reconsideration decision) — implied resolved by Jacob if this ticket exists
- New ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for the shared bot (separate from picortex's, in case we need to revoke)
notes:
## Open decisions resolved 2026-06-01 (defaults — minimize change)

1. **Bot identity: keep `picortex_bot_7ecd2883dbd5ceef`.** Preserves every existing message authorship row in Neo4j; conversation memberships survive the swap; existing JWT minted off OpenChat's JWT_SECRET can be reused as-is (no JWT re-issue dance). Rename can come later if we ever want to.

2. **Bot display name: keep 'picortex'.** Existing @mention trigger keeps working — anyone in a group who's already typing '@picortex' doesn't need to relearn. The name baggage is real but doesn't block anything; we can do a name change separately as a one-shot Neo4j UPDATE once we feel like it.

Both choices = 'don't change things you don't need to change.' Step 4 of the deploy can copy picortex's .env values straight in (OPENCHAT_BOT_JWT, BOT_NAME=picortex). The only fresh secret is the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (so revoking it doesn't break picortex's Linq side during cutover).

title: Discovery + email privacy hardening (DEFERRED — for launch readiness, not now)
description:
## Why DEFERRED

Jacob 2026-06-03: 'for the future, but not right now since we're still testing — probably not necessarily listing out all of the users on the service, but I don't wanna change that yet — and also like not explicitly listing out their emails.'

This is intentionally deferred until broader launch readiness. During internal/F&F testing the current 'see everyone, see their emails' behavior is acceptable because the user pool is small + trusted. Before opening signups to the public this needs to change.

## Two distinct issues to address

### 1. Default discoverability — don't list all users on the service

Today (likely surface: NewConversationScreen, search results, contact picker) the app surfaces every user on the platform when you go to start a new chat. For a small private group this is fine; at any scale it becomes:
- A privacy issue (random people can browse the user list)
- A spam vector (mass-DM bots)
- A bad UX (overwhelming list of people you don't know)

After hardening, users should be discoverable ONLY via:
- Existing 1:1 or group conversation membership
- Mutual group membership
- Contacts match (OpenChat-3ag.2 — once that ships)
- QR scan / direct invite link (already supported)
- Explicit search by exact username/handle (NOT by partial fuzzy across all users)

### 2. Don't surface emails in lists / pickers

Today (likely SearchScreen, NewConversationScreen, ContactProfileScreen, possibly mentions UI) users' emails are shown alongside their display name. Email is PII that:
- Many users don't want public
- Enables impersonation / phishing reconnaissance
- Provides minimal UX value once a username/handle exists

After hardening:
- Email visible only on YOUR OWN profile (and to admin/internal tooling)
- Display name + handle + avatar are the canonical identifiers shown to others
- If a user wants their email findable, they can opt in (add it to a 'contact info' section of their profile)

## Depends on / related

- OpenChat-3ag.2 (contacts-based discovery — must ship BEFORE removing the 'browse all users' affordance, or users will have NO way to find new people)
- OpenChat-d8w (App Privacy nutrition labels — will need to be updated to reflect tightened email visibility)
- A handles/usernames system may need to exist first if it doesn't already

## When to claim

Only after:
- OpenChat-3ag.2 (contacts discovery) ships, AND
- F&F testing is winding down + onboarding to public is planned

Until then, do NOT change current behavior. This ticket exists only to make sure the work isn't forgotten when the time comes.
notes: Deferred until OpenChat-3ag.2 (contacts discovery) ships AND public-launch planning starts. Jacob explicitly: 'not right now since we're still testing'.

title: Decision: phone-number sign-in (WhatsApp-style)?
description:
DECISION ticket, not implementation. Decide whether/when to add SMS-OTP sign-in alongside Google OAuth.

CURRENT STATE: Google OAuth only (iOS + web). No phoneNumber field on :User. ~5 users.

TRADEOFF MATRIX:
| Dim                       | Google (today) | Phone+OTP                | Both                |
|---------------------------|----------------|--------------------------|---------------------|
| Onboarding friction       | Medium         | Low                      | Low                 |
| Cost                      | $0            | $0.005-0.04/SMS         | Marginal            |
| Dev/test                  | Easy           | Hard                     | Hard                |
| Abuse surface             | Low            | SIM swap, toll fraud     | Both                |
| Contacts matching         | Useless        | High value               | High value          |
| Portability               | Stable         | Numbers recycle          | Both                |
| iOS App Store             | Fine           | Triggers SIWA req        | SIWA req            |
| Time-to-ship              | N/A            | 1-2 weeks                | Same                |

RECOMMENDATION: DEFER. Stay Google-only for ~3 months. Revisit triggers:
  (a) >100 users AND contacts-matching is top growth lever, OR
  (b) Specific repeat user blocked by no-Google option.

WHEN BUILT: use Twilio Verify (not raw Programmable SMS) + add Sign in with Apple simultaneously (App Store rule). Design account-merge UX BEFORE first SMS goes out.

DO-NOW PREP (low effort, future-proofs):
- [ ] Add nullable phoneNumber (E.164) + phoneNumberVerifiedAt fields to :User in Neo4j (no migration needed)
- [ ] Add phoneNumberHash (sha256(E.164)) index

ACCEPTANCE:
- [ ] Decision documented in resolution comment
- [ ] If 'defer': close with rationale + revisit-trigger; phoneNumber field added prophylactically
- [ ] If 'build now': spawn epic with sub-tickets for Twilio Verify wiring, SIWA, account-merge UX, abuse controls
close_reason: Decision shipped 2026-06-01 in docs/decisions/2026-06-01-phone-sign-in.md: DEFER phone-number sign-in. Stay Google + Apple-only until specific triggers fire (>100 users + contacts-matching as top growth lever; named user blocked by no-Google option; or contacts-driven growth pivot). Zero-cost prep: Neo4j user_phone_hash index added in server/src/db.ts for future-proofing.

title: Real-time sidebar updates and unread message indicators
description:
**Problem:**
Two related issues with message notifications and real-time updates:

1. **Sidebar doesn't update for non-active conversations**
   - When you have conversation A open and receive a message in conversation B, the sidebar doesn't show that B has new messages
   - No unread badge/indicator appears
   - Conversation order doesn't update to show most recent at top
   - Have to click on the conversation to see there's a new message

2. **New contact messages require page refresh**
   - When someone new messages you, it doesn't appear in the conversation list
   - Must refresh the entire page to see the new conversation

**What's idiomatic in chat apps (Slack, Discord, WhatsApp, Messenger):**

1. **Unread indicators:**
   - Red dot/badge with unread count on conversations
   - Bold text for conversation name when unread
   - Preview text shows latest message

2. **Conversation list behavior:**
   - Conversations reorder in real-time (most recent at top)
   - New conversations appear automatically at top
   - Visual highlight/animation when new message arrives

3. **Real-time updates via WebSocket:**
   - Already have WebSocket for messages in active chat
   - Need to also push updates to sidebar state
   - When message received for conversation X: update X's lastMessage, lastMessageAt, unreadCount

**Implementation approach:**

1. **State management:**
   - Track unreadCount per conversation
   - Update when: message received for non-active conversation
   - Clear when: user opens that conversation

2. **WebSocket events:**
   - On new_message event: update the affected conversation in sidebar state
   - On new_conversation event: add to conversation list

3. **UI components:**
   - Add unread badge component to ConversationListItem
   - Sort conversations by lastMessageAt (descending)
   - Highlight/animate on new message

**Affects:** Core chat UX - users expect real-time updates in any modern chat app
close_reason: v1 shipped (45f9b80). Client-side unreadByConv Map in ChatContext, bumped in handleMessage when conv is non-active and sender isn't self, cleared in setActiveConversation. ConversationList renders a blue pill (99+ cap) + bolder weight for unread rows. Real-time sidebar reorder was already in place from the 401-cascade work (handleMessage re-sorts conversations on every inbound). v2 — server-side lastReadAt + cross-device sync — left as follow-up, not blocking. Stretch animation/highlight per ticket also deferred.

title: Group chats: share a group conversation with an agent (agent as full member/controller)
description:
## What

Make agents first-class participants in group chats. Should be as simple as inviting a human to a group — add the agent (by its registered Agent Key / Agent User ID) to the conversation, and that agent can read messages, send messages, react, set group topic, and otherwise act on the group like any other member.

Use cases (Jacob's framing):
- Spin up a planning group with a couple of teammates + an agent that summarizes / takes notes / drafts replies
- Add an agent to an existing group later, it has the full conversation history visible (with maybe a soft 'recent messages only' default if the history is very long)
- Multiple agents in the same group (writing partner + research bot + scheduler bot — they coordinate via the group)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Group settings UI: 'Add member' → option to pick from registered Agent Keys (mine), or invite a public agent by handle / paste their agent ID
- [ ] Server: existing participant-add flow accepts agent users; agent users have a flag isAgent=true on the User node
- [ ] Permissions: by default, an agent added to a group has the same permissions as a regular member (read + write + react). Admin-only actions (rename group, remove members) require the agent to be promoted to admin explicitly.
- [ ] When an agent is added: an automatic system message in the group ('🤖 Jacob added @WritingAssistant to the group') — same as for humans, with agent indicator
- [ ] Agent can leave a group (or owner can remove it) using the same mechanisms
- [ ] Read receipts work — when the agent has 'seen' messages, the receipt updates like for humans
- [ ] Mute / focus / @-mention rules apply the same way; @-mentioning an agent in a group triggers a guaranteed delivery and (if push exists for the agent's owner) the owner sees activity

## Related

- OpenChat-3kr (Thoughts epic), OpenChat-3kr.3 (Agentic features — summon-an-agent UI, automation rules) — relates but distinct
- OpenChat-ham (Per-user agent identity) — depends on this work
- OpenChat-sju, OpenChat-sgb (openchat-agent deploy) — the runtime that hosts the agents

## Open

- Read access to history: full history vs only-from-when-joined? Default to only-from-when-joined for new agent members; allow group admin to grant full history if needed.
- Agent rate-limits in groups: should an agent's send rate be throttled differently than a human's, given they can produce more messages? Default to same rate-limit as humans for now; revisit.
- Mention syntax: how to disambiguate '@WritingAssistant' across multiple agents with similar names? Agent IDs as fallback in the mention picker.

title: Mobile/China-VPN users can't send: websocket-only transport + no send queue
description: Lucy (mobile, China VPN) cannot send messages. Root cause: client pins Socket.IO to transports:['websocket'] (no polling fallback) and sendMessage rejects with 'Not connected' the instant the socket is down — no queue/retry. Mobile backgrounding + VPN/GFW reset the WS constantly, so sends land in the disconnected gap and silently drop. Fix: (1) queue-and-retry sends, (2) re-enable polling fallback with WS upgrade, (3) reconnect on visibilitychange. Preserve OpenChat-0kv Cloudflare WS fix.
notes: Root causes: (1) REST POST /conversations/:id/messages never emitted message:new, so socket-down sends (mobile/China VPN) were invisible to recipients. (2) message:send ack had no timeout -> on mobile the Promise hung forever and the REST fallback never fired. Fixed both + MessageInput restores text/toasts on hard failure + useChatSocket reconnects on visibilitychange/online/focus. Transport left websocket-only to preserve OpenChat-0kv. Builds clean. Commit 4908c0b.

Also: (2) broadcast message:new to each participant's user:<id> room so recipients who haven't joined the conversation room still get it live; (3) dedupe the manual setMessages append in ChatContext catch; (4) add an AbortController timeout to the REST send so the hard-failure path can't hang on mobile/VPN.

title: [decision] Agent heartbeat → outbound notifications to hooks: native vs external personal agent
description:
A periodic 'heartbeat' where the agent proactively reviews state (important new messages, triage results, reminders, things needing attention) and pushes notifications OUT to hooks — webhooks, push, Slack, the user's other channels.

KEY DECISION (the reason this is a [decision] ticket): implement natively in OpenChat vs rely on the user's EXTERNAL personal agent.
- NATIVE: server-side per-user scheduler + webhook/notification dispatch. Works for everyone out-of-box; we own the scheduler + inference cost + reliability.
- EXTERNAL: the user's own personal agent polls OpenChat's API on its schedule and decides what to notify (fits the Shipper 'your app is a tool the agent calls' thesis). More personalized + offloads cost, but only works for users who HAVE a personal agent.

RECOMMENDATION TO EVALUATE: do BOTH — expose the API/event surface (a webhook/events feed + 'what needs attention' endpoint) so external agents can drive it, AND ship a lightweight native heartbeat for users without a personal agent. Depends on the access-control model (openchat-j0o) and the triage feature (bfn inbound-triage). Decide before building.

title: [EPIC] Ambient agents in every chat + bot data-access/privacy model
description:
VISION (Jacob 2026-06-04): an AI agent implicitly present in every chat (yours + others'); bots present in group chats; ability to message someone's bot explicitly; your assistant can cause another's bot to kick something off. Open question: per-user agents ('Jacob's agent' + the other person's agent) vs ONE general useful agent with skills (e.g. NVC mediation as a built-in skill). 

THE CRUX = bot DATA ACCESS / PRIVACY. Must not add your bot to a group and leak personal data. Reference models to mirror: Cortex (total isolation), Noos (private/public/group node visibility), WikiHub (public/public-edit/private/unlisted + teams/grants), Notestream (groups), Collura (?). Idea: tiered access control (private / group-or-team-scoped / public); the agent's data access = union of what the CURRENT context is allowed to see (group chat → only group+public, never your private); approval workflow for the bot to use/send private data; separate scoped memory per bot/context.

MINIMAL DEMO ('poor man's version'): apply the same visibility model (public / group / private) to the OpenChat Thoughtstream THOUGHTS already in-app — a small, concrete demonstration of the access-control behavior.

This epic is DESIGN-FIRST: research prior art across Jacob's projects, then a written design (data model, access-control rules, agent-context scoping, messaging-a-bot UX, NVC-skill plugin model, approval workflow), then phased build starting with the Thoughts-visibility demo.

In-app 'update available' banner for NATIVE binary bumps: app checks a backend/version endpoint (or EAS Update manifest) comparing runtimeVersion/build vs latest available; non-intrusive banner -> deep link to TestFlight/App Store. Per global rule 'Update Available Indicator': visible not intrusive, one-click, non-blocking.
Pitfalls: OTA can't ship native module changes; runtimeVersion must bump when native changes; don't OTA-push a JS bundle incompatible with the installed native runtime.

title: Make local-build.sh self-heal Node version (don't rely on machine-local .xcode.env.local)
description:
TestFlight build failed twice with 'Unable to resolve module index.ts' because the Xcode 'Bundle React Native code and images' phase ran under Node 25 (brew auto-bumped the unversioned node keg). Expo SDK 54/RN 0.81/Metro need Node 20/22/24.

Key gotcha: the Xcode build phase sources ios/.xcode.env which does NODE_BINARY=$(command -v node) in a PATH-sanitized shell — so prepending node@22 to PATH in the launching shell does NOT reach the phase. Fix that worked: ios/.xcode.env.local with 'export NODE_BINARY=/opt/homebrew/opt/node@22/bin/node'. But that file is machine-local + gitignored, so other machines/agents will hit this again.

Durable fix options (pick one):
1. local-build.sh detects $(node -v) major not in {20,22,24} and writes ios/.xcode.env.local pinning to an installed LTS (brew --prefix node@22) before building.
2. Commit a versioned .xcode.env that prefers node@22 if present.
3. Add an engines/Volta pin + docs.
Recommend option 1 (self-healing script). Also pinned repo via .node-version=22 (committed) — but Xcode's NODE_BINARY ignores .node-version, hence the script guard.
notes: TRUE root cause of headless build failure is NOT node — it's TMPDIR. Claude Code's TMPDIR=/tmp/claude-501 causes a /tmp vs /private/tmp symlink mismatch that breaks Metro's absolute --entry-file resolution. Durable fix for local-build.sh: at the top, if TMPDIR resolves under /tmp, re-point it to a canonical /private/tmp dir (mkdir -p /private/tmp/ocbuild; export TMPDIR=/private/tmp/ocbuild). Combine with the node@22 LTS guard. Then headless/agent (nohup) builds work without NoMachine.
close_reason: Added TMPDIR + Node self-heal guards to local-build.sh (openchat-mobile commit). TMPDIR repin to $HOME/.ocbuild-tmp was the real fix (avoids /tmp<->/private/tmp Metro resolution bug); Node-LTS PATH guard as secondary. Headless nohup build now archives + submits to TestFlight without NoMachine. Verified v0.1.14 build 71.

title: Forward-to-my-agent: long-press any message in any chat to privately send it to my Assistant
description:
Idea (Jacob 2026-06-04): from EVERY conversation at all times, let me tag/forward a specific message to my own Assistant agent privately — e.g. long-press a message → 'Ask my agent' / 'Forward to Assistant' → it lands in my private Assistant DM (only I see it) with the original message as context, so I can ask the agent to act on it (summarize, draft a reply, remember it, file feedback, search related, etc.) without the other participants knowing.

Design considerations to weigh:
- ENTRY POINT: message action menu (long-press mobile / hover menu web) item 'Ask my agent' or 'Forward to Assistant'. Possibly also an always-present affordance (a persistent '@agent' you can tag inline in any message — but inline @agent in a shared convo risks leaking to others, so the long-press→private-forward path is the privacy-safe default).
- PRIVACY: the forward must go to the user's OWN Assistant DM (containsBot self-conversation), NOT post into the shared conversation. The other participants must never see it. Carry a reference {sourceConversationId, sourceMessageId, quoted content} so the Assistant has context.
- TWO MODES likely: (a) 'Forward to Assistant' (just drops the message into the Assistant DM as quoted context), (b) 'Ask my agent about this' (forwards + prompts for a question). 
- INLINE @agent (stretch): typing @agent / #agent in a shared message could trigger the bot to reply — but only privately to the tagger, or visibly to all? Decide. Inline-visible @agent = a shared AI helper (different product surface). Keep separate from the private forward.

- Parity: implement in apps/mobile (long-press) AND apps/web (hover menu). Backend: a small endpoint POST /api/assistant/forward { sourceConversationId, sourceMessageId, question? } that injects the quoted context into the user's Assistant DM and triggers a turn.

title: Enforce read/write scopes in resolveActor (agent keys)
description:
Agent keys store read/write scopes (server/src/routes/agentKeys.ts) but resolveActor authenticates WITHOUT enforcing them per-route — a 'read-only' key can currently write. Flagged by Codex during the connect-agent merge (2026-06-04).

Pre-existing on the investigate-url-sync-issue-2 branch, not introduced by the merge. Currently errs toward MORE capability, which is acceptable per Jacob's 'agent should be able to do everything' stance — but scope toggles in the UI are misleading until enforced.

Fix: in resolveActor, after resolving the key, attach its scopes to req; add a requireScope('write') guard on mutating chat routes (POST/PATCH/DELETE messages, POST conversations, participants). Read routes require 'read'. Keep default keys read+write so nothing breaks.

title: Thoughts: new thought should appear instantly (live socket insert), not only on refresh
description: Ordering is already newest-first (ORDER BY createdAt DESC) and the data confirms new tags create thoughts at the top — but there's a race: tag-extraction is async (fires a beat after send), so if the user switches to the Thoughts tab immediately, the focus-refresh can run BEFORE the thought exists, and it only shows on a later pull-to-refresh. Fix: emit a socket event when a thought is created (like message:transcript) and have the Thoughts screen prepend it live. Also confirm older native builds get the current focus-refresh behavior via a rebuild.
